overall_summary: Crypto faces mixed drivers today as strong spot Bitcoin ETF inflows offer support while corporate BTC sales and a stalled CLARITY Act weigh on sentiment. Hopes for a Hormuz deal are pulling yields lower and lifting risk assets, yet ongoing geopolitical flares from Russia and China keep caution in place. Traders are watching upcoming labor data for the next macro catalyst.
key_points: Spot Bitcoin ETFs post solid $211M inflows
CLARITY Act stalls near Senate deadline
Yields drop on Hormuz deal hopes
Geopolitical risks elevated by Russia and China

items.title: Coldcard Hack Hits ~$120M, Sparks Custody Scramble
items.summary: A firmware flaw in Coldcard hardware wallets has led to roughly one hundred twenty million dollars in Bitcoin stolen across multiple waves since late July, with the attack still ongoing according to on-chain trackers. The incident is flooding Bitcoin's mempool with transactions as users rush to move coins, pushing active addresses and whale transfers to multi-month highs. Traders should care because it is hammering confidence in self-custody hardware while simultaneously boosting the case for regulated ETFs and exchange custody, and the market has so far absorbed the selling without a major breakdown.
items.impact: Near-term fear and potential ETF/CEX inflow tailwind if self-custody exodus continues

items.title: Spot Bitcoin ETFs Post $211M Inflow on August 4
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded two hundred eleven point five million dollars in net inflows on August fourth, following one hundred seventy million the prior session for roughly three hundred eighty million over two days. BlackRock's IBIT led the buying. This matters for traders because it shows institutional demand is quietly returning even as price chops around sixty-four thousand and headlines stay negative, providing a real bid under the market.
items.impact: Supports price stability and potential upside if inflows persist

items.title: Strategy Sells Another 1,638 BTC for $105 Million
items.summary: Michael Saylor's Strategy disclosed selling one thousand six hundred thirty-eight Bitcoin last week for about one hundred five million dollars at an average of roughly sixty-four thousand, below its seventy-five thousand average cost basis. Proceeds went toward preferred dividends and buybacks while the firm still holds over eight hundred forty-two thousand BTC and has built a four billion dollar cash reserve. Traders need to watch this because repeated sales from the largest corporate holder chip away at the never-sell treasury narrative and add incremental supply overhang.
items.impact: Negative narrative and mild supply pressure on Bitcoin

items.title: CLARITY Act Stalls as Senate Recess Deadline Nears
items.summary: The Digital Asset Market Clarity Act is stuck short of the votes needed in the Senate, tangled in ethics questions around Trump crypto holdings and other riders, with passage odds sliding sharply. Congress is heading into an August tenth recess, leaving little time. This is key for traders because clear SEC-CFTC rules have been priced as a major structural positive; further delay keeps regulatory overhang alive and removes a potential catalyst into the fall midterms.
items.impact: Prolongs regulatory uncertainty, capping risk appetite

items.title: Hashdex to Liquidate Tiny $14.7M Bitcoin ETF
items.summary: Hashdex is closing and liquidating its US spot Bitcoin ETF DEFI after it only gathered about fourteen point seven million in assets. Trading ends mid-August and remaining Bitcoin holdings will be sold for cash distributions to shareholders. It is a small fund so the direct sell pressure is negligible, but it highlights how scale is everything in the ETF space and that weaker products are being culled while giants like IBIT keep pulling flows.
items.impact: Minimal direct price impact; underscores winner-take-most ETF dynamics

items.title: SpaceX Marks $540M Drop in Bitcoin Holdings Value
items.summary: In its first public earnings as a listed company, SpaceX reported holding roughly eighteen thousand seven hundred Bitcoin whose carrying value fell about five hundred forty million dollars in the first half on the price decline. The company beat revenue estimates but the mark-down was notable. Traders should note it because SpaceX is one of the larger known corporate Bitcoin holders and the disclosure keeps institutional balance-sheet exposure in the headlines without any indication of selling.
items.impact: No new supply; reinforces corporate BTC as volatile balance-sheet asset

items.title: Treasury Yields Drop on Hormuz Deal Hopes
items.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield eased to around 4.61 percent as reports of a possible interim US-Iran deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz pushed oil prices lower. This eased inflation worries and cut September Fed hike odds toward 57 percent from higher levels. Crypto traders should care because falling yields and softer dollar pressure often support risk assets like Bitcoin by improving liquidity conditions and reducing tight-policy fears.
items.impact: Lower yields and reduced hike odds support risk-on moves in crypto and equities

items.title: ISM Manufacturing PMI Hits 55.6, Strongest Since 2022
items.summary: July ISM manufacturing PMI jumped to 55.6 from 53.3, beating the 54 consensus and marking the fastest factory expansion in over four years. Production surged, new orders held firm, and employment returned to expansion at 52.8, helped by AI investment and front-loading amid geopolitical risks. Traders watch this because robust growth data keeps the economy resilient but elevated prices could sustain hawkish Fed pressure.
items.impact: Supports growth narrative yet keeps rate-hike risks alive ahead of more data

items.title: JOLTS Job Openings Fall to 7.359 Million in June
items.summary: US job openings dropped 178,000 to 7.359 million, below the 7.4 million forecast, with big declines in healthcare. Hiring rose and layoffs stayed low, pointing to a stable but cooling labor market in slow-hire slow-fire mode. This matters for traders as softer demand could ease Fed tightening bets while still-solid conditions limit aggressive dovish shifts before Friday's payrolls.
items.impact: Mixed labor signal that trims extreme hike odds without confirming weakness

items.title: US Trade Deficit Narrows to $73.3 Billion in June
items.summary: The goods and services trade gap shrank to 73.3 billion dollars from a revised 77.6 billion as imports fell more than exports. Goods imports dropped notably in capital and consumer categories. Crypto and macro traders track this for clues on domestic demand and growth contribution, especially with AI-related trade flows in play.
items.impact: Mildly positive for growth optics but secondary to labor and Fed signals

items.title: Factory Orders Unexpectedly Drop 0.3 Percent in June
items.summary: New orders for manufactured goods fell 0.3 percent after a revised steeper drop prior, missing expectations for a small gain. Demand elsewhere held up with AI infrastructure investment providing support. This soft print adds to the mixed data picture heading into key labor reports that will shape near-term rate expectations.
items.impact: Slightly cooler activity signal that balances stronger PMI readings

items.title: Key Labor Data Due Today: ADP and ISM Services
items.summary: Markets await July ADP private payrolls expected around 70,000 after 98,000 prior, plus final S&P services PMI and ISM services PMI around 54.5. Fed Governor Cook also speaks later. These feed directly into Friday NFP expectations and September FOMC pricing under a divided Fed that held rates at 3.5 to 3.75 percent last meeting. Traders should care as surprises here can swing yields, the dollar, and risk appetite sharply.
items.impact: High-volatility catalyst that will reset Fed path odds before NFP

items.title: Trump Hails 'Very Good' Iran Talks; Hormuz Deal Hopes Rise
items.summary: President Trump said the US had all-day negotiations with Iran and that the Strait of Hormuz will reopen very soon, with officials eyeing a possible interim deal announcement. Mediators including Qatar and Oman report progress, even as Tehran denies direct talks and links any agreement to an end to US threats. Oil prices extended declines and stocks hit records on the de-escalation hopes. Traders should watch closely because a real reopening of the strait would ease the biggest energy supply risk premium of the year and support risk assets including Bitcoin.
items.impact: Lower oil and risk-on move if deal materializes

items.title: Russia Launches Major Ballistic Missile Barrage on Kyiv
items.summary: Russian forces hit Kyiv and the surrounding region overnight with dozens of ballistic missiles, cruise missiles and drones, killing at least 15 to 17 people and injuring more than 40. Fires broke out across multiple districts and warehouses. This continues the pattern of heavy strikes as the war grinds on with no diplomatic off-ramp. For markets it keeps European energy and defense spending elevated and adds to overall geopolitical risk that can pressure risk assets when combined with Middle East uncertainty.
items.impact: Elevated risk premium and European volatility

items.title: US Has Used Virtually All Long-Range Precision Missiles
items.summary: Reuters reports the US Army has expended virtually all of its ATACMS and Precision Strike Missile stockpiles during the five-month Iran war, plus a large share of Tomahawks and air-defense interceptors. Officials worry this limits options for further large-scale strikes and readiness against other adversaries. Trump downplayed the issue saying production is ramping. This matters because it could force riskier tactics or constrain US freedom of action, prolonging Middle East uncertainty and oil volatility that weighs on crypto risk appetite.
items.impact: Higher chance of drawn-out conflict and munitions scarcity premium

items.title: China Hits Back with Drone Export Curbs and US Firm Sanctions
items.summary: Beijing tightened export controls on drones to the United States and sanctioned multiple American companies in retaliation for recent US tech and telecom restrictions. The moves target dual-use technology and supply chains already strained by the broader rivalry. This escalates the tech and trade cold war at a moment when global supply chains are sensitive. Crypto traders should note it as another source of risk-off pressure and potential inflation via disrupted components.
items.impact: Trade and tech tension weighing on global risk assets

items.title: US Revokes Visa of Brazilian Ambassador in Diplomatic Spat
items.summary: The Trump administration revoked the visa of Brazil's ambassador to Washington in response to Brasilia delaying approval of the US envoy and denying visas to American diplomats ahead of Brazil's October election. Brazil called the justifications false. The move deepens friction between the two largest economies in the Americas. While not an immediate market mover, it adds to political uncertainty in a key emerging market and commodity exporter that crypto traders monitor for broader risk sentiment.
items.impact: Limited direct market hit but signals rising bilateral friction

items.title: Shipping Attacks Persist as Hormuz and Red Sea Remain Disrupted
items.summary: A projectile struck a vessel near the Strait of Hormuz and an Indian-flagged cargo ship was sunk near Yemeni waters with all crew rescued; Houthis continue their blockade and claims of attacks on Saudi-linked shipping. Traffic through key chokepoints stays heavily restricted despite diplomatic talk. These incidents keep insurance costs high and force longer routes, supporting oil prices on the margin even as deal hopes pull them lower. Traders care because unresolved shipping risks can reverse the recent oil sell-off and keep volatility elevated for risk assets.
items.impact: Persistent energy and shipping risk premium
